8	// :opt_update<Opt>) implemented only 4 optimizers (AdamW/Lion/Muon/SuperGrok15)

14	// function from csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h (the canonical optimizer component —
15	// the same device functions the per-op launchers compile). No fallback, no
16	// templating one optimizer from another, no toy substitute. Each optimizer's
17	// genuine state buffers are plumbed through FusedOptState.

20	//   The L3 megakernel fuses the per-element optimizer TAIL after fwd+bwd. The
21	//   multi-phase OUTER parts that are not per-element — Muon's Newton–Schulz
22	//   orthogonalization, Prodigy's global d reduction, LookSAM's perturb/restore
23	//   ascent, SG11/SG15's cosine-gate reduction, and SG2's CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net
24	//   — run as their own launch(es) and hand this tail the precomputed result
25	//   (orth direction, d factor, sam_dir, reduced gate, smart-grad). This mirrors
26	//   the real per-op pipelines exactly; the tail math below IS the real apply.

54	    AdamW = 0, Lion = 1, Grokfast = 2, GrokAdamW = 3, LookSAM = 4,

60	// per-op neuralgrok kernel's default instantiation.
61	static constexpr int kPsiHidden = 16;

64	// neuralgrok has no per-element `extra` n-slice (its psi-net is a small
65	// per-TENSOR weight set), so the cell repurposes the otherwise-unused `extra`

67	//   extra[0                  .. kPsiHidden)        = psi_W1  [kPsiHidden]
68	//   extra[kPsiHidden         .. 2*kPsiHidden)      = psi_b1  [kPsiHidden]
69	//   extra[2*kPsiHidden       .. 3*kPsiHidden)      = psi_W2  [kPsiHidden]

76	static constexpr int kPsiB1Off = kPsiHidden;
77	static constexpr int kPsiW2Off = 2 * kPsiHidden;

86	// sharpness) and H=32. An SG11/SG15 cell carries this weight pack in the head of a
87	// dedicated state slice (host-scattered each step, like NeuralGrok's psi pack):
88	//   phi[0           .. 2*H)            = phi_W1 [H,2]  (row-major: [j*2], [j*2+1])
89	//   phi[2*H         .. 3*H)            = phi_b1 [H]
90	//   phi[3*H         .. 4*H)            = phi_W2 [H]
91	//   phi[4*H]                          = phi_b2 (scalar; read on-device)

93	// null-deref) and reads phi_b2 on-device from sg_phi_W2[H] (a host scalar cannot

95	static constexpr int kSgPhiHidden = 32;
96	static constexpr int kSgPhiW1Off  = 0;
97	static constexpr int kSgPhiB1Off  = 2 * kSgPhiHidden;
98	static constexpr int kSgPhiW2Off  = 3 * kSgPhiHidden;
99	static constexpr int kSgPhiB2Off  = 4 * kSgPhiHidden;   // scalar slot (device-side)

105	struct FusedOptState {

107	    float* exp_avg     = nullptr;   // m
108	    float* exp_avg_sq  = nullptr;   // v
109	    // Grokfast / GrokAdamW slow-gradient EMA.

113	    // Prodigy trajectory accumulator + adaptive d (scalar, host/reduce-stage).

115	    float  d_factor    = 1.0f;
116	    // SG11/SG15 momentum buffer + reduced cosine/accuracy gate (scalar).
117	    float* mu          = nullptr;
118	    float  gate        = 1.0f;
119	    // Muon precomputed Newton–Schulz orthogonalized direction + step scales.

121	    float  neg_lr_scale = 0.0f;
122	    float  decay_factor = 1.0f;
123	    // NeuralGrok psi-net (per-tensor MLP weights) — psi computed per element.
124	    const float* psi_W1 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
125	    const float* psi_b1 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
126	    const float* psi_W2 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
127	    float        psi_b2 = 0.0f;
128	    // SG2 smart-grad from the CSA/HCA meta-net launch (drives the Adam tail).
129	    const float* smart_grad = nullptr;
130	    // Shared hyperparameters.
131	    float lr = 1e-3f, beta1 = 0.9f, beta2 = 0.999f, eps = 1e-8f, wd = 0.01f;
132	    float bc1 = 1.0f, bc2 = 1.0f;       // un-inverted bias-corrections
133	    float alpha = 0.98f, beta = 0.0f, lamb = 2.0f, alpha_max = 1.0f;
134	    // GrokAdamW (decoder L3-TC conversion): layer-wise β1 decay rate γ + global
135	    // grad-norm clip threshold. clip_coef is DEVICE-computed once per launch (the
136	    // global grad-norm reduction in P2.5) and stashed here; it passes through
137	    // rebase_state unchanged (a scalar). Defaults are the inert no-op (γ=0 ⇒ a
138	    // single global β1; grad_clip<=0 ⇒ no clip; clip_coef=1 ⇒ grad unscaled).
139	    float gamma = 0.0f, grad_clip = 0.0f, clip_coef = 1.0f;
140	    // Prodigy (decoder L3-TC conversion, STAGED global-d). The d-estimate's
141	    // INPUTS that the in-kernel reduction stage (fused_decoder_megakernel_tc's
142	    // Prodigy branch, between B2 and P3) consumes/produces:
143	    //   * param_init — the trajectory anchor p0 (flat blob parallel to params),
144	    //     seeded = params at step 1 by the host; r = Σ d²·<g, p0−p> needs it.
145	    //     rebase_state offsets it per tensor (added below).
146	    //   * d0 / d_coef / beta3 — the estimator scalars (host-bound via FusedScalars):
147	    //     d0 seeds d_prev at step 1 (the persisted d_lr slot zero-inits to 0, but
148	    //     eager inits _d_lr=d0=1e-6 — the cold-start the single-step gate needs);

153	    //     stage decays + accumulates + writes d back each step). NOT rebased.
154	    // st.s_track (Prodigy's `s` buffer) + st.d_factor (the reduced d the apply

156	    const float* param_init = nullptr;
157	    float* prodigy_persist  = nullptr;   // [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]  (persisted)
158	    float d0 = 1e-6f, d_coef = 1.0f, beta3 = 0.0f;

160	    // hyperparameters (eager adamw_lr/adamw_betas, muon.py:115-125). The 2D group's
161	    // lr/momentum ride the main lr/beta1 fields (P2.7 NS + apply); the 1D AdamW
162	    // tail (P3) reads aux_lr/aux_beta1/aux_beta2 instead (bc1/bc2 device-computed

165	    float aux_lr = 1e-3f, aux_beta1 = 0.9f, aux_beta2 = 0.98f;
166	    // LookSAM (decoder/vit/mamba L3-TC, MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward). rho is the
167	    // perturbation radius; the model phase computes rho_over_norm = rho/‖g‖_global
168	    // ON-DEVICE (same deterministic ascending-CTA reduction as GrokAdamW's P2.5),
169	    // perturbs p'=p+rho_over_norm·g, runs a SECOND in-kernel fwd+bwd at p' → g_sam,

176	    // cell is byte-identical.

180	    // `sharpness = (g_sam − g)²` (NOT looksam's sam_dir = g_sam − g; the elementwise
181	    // write differs — supergrok11_sm90.cuh:246 / supergrok15_sm90.cuh:315), persisted

258	//  Defaults here reproduce the OLD inert behavior EXACTLY (bc=gate=d_factor=1,
259	//  decay_factor=1, the same beta/eps/wd/alpha defaults), so a caller that does
260	//  not pass scalars yields byte-identical results to the pre-fix cells — the
261	//  widening is additive, not a behavior change for unset fields.
262	//
263	//  Per-tensor step count / bias correction (loud assumption): the megakernel
264	//  treats the whole flat param as ONE task, so a SINGLE (bc1, bc2) pair is bound
265	//  per call. That is correct ONLY when every parameter tensor shares the same
266	//  step counter — which holds in the grokking race (all params step together
267	//  every iteration). The host computes bc1 = 1 - beta1^step, bc2 = 1 - beta2^step
268	//  from that shared step and passes them here. If a future caller steps tensors
269	//  at different counts, it must call fused_step per-tensor with that tensor's bc.
270	// =========================================================================
271	struct FusedScalars {
272	    float lr           = 1e-3f;
273	    float beta1        = 0.9f;
274	    float beta2        = 0.999f;
275	    float eps          = 1e-8f;
276	    float wd           = 0.01f;
277	    float bc1          = 1.0f;   // 1 - beta1^step (un-inverted; apply divides)
278	    float bc2          = 1.0f;   // 1 - beta2^step (un-inverted; apply divides)
279	    float alpha        = 0.98f;  // meta-net strength / grokfast_alpha / neuralgrok alpha
280	    float beta         = 0.0f;   // neuralgrok beta (affine psi term)
281	    float lamb         = 2.0f;   // grokfast/grokadamw amplification (grokfast_lamb)
282	    float alpha_max    = 1.0f;   // SG15 per-coord alpha clip ceiling
283	    float gate         = 1.0f;   // SG11 cosine gate / SG15 sigmoid(accuracy) gate
284	    float d_factor     = 1.0f;   // Prodigy adaptive d (effective LR scale)
285	    float neg_lr_scale = 0.0f;   // Muon: -lr * ns_scale (2D NS-orth apply)
286	    float decay_factor = 1.0f;   // Muon: 1 - lr*wd (decoupled decay multiplier)
287	    // ── GrokAdamW append-only widening (decoder L3-TC conversion). Both default
288	    //    to the INERT value (0.0 ⇒ disabled), so every other cell is byte-identical
289	    //    (additive ABI, same contract as the original C2-gap widening above).
290	    float gamma     = 0.0f;   // GrokAdamW layer-wise β1 decay rate: β1_i=β1*(1-γ)^i
291	    float grad_clip = 0.0f;   // GrokAdamW global grad-norm clip (<=0 ⇒ no clip)
292	    // ── Prodigy append-only widening (decoder L3-TC conversion, STAGED global-d).
293	    //    The estimator scalars; defaults are eager/inert so every other cell is
294	    //    byte-identical. d0 seeds d_prev at step 1; beta3=sqrt(β2) decays the
295	    //    persisted (r_ema,s_ema); d_coef scales the candidate d (1 ⇒ no scale).
296	    float d0     = 1e-6f;     // Prodigy d0 (step-1 d_prev cold-start)
297	    float d_coef = 1.0f;      // Prodigy d_coef (candidate-d scale)
298	    float beta3  = 0.0f;      // Prodigy EMA decay = sqrt(beta2) (0 ⇒ no persistence)
299	    // ── Muon append-only widening (ViT L3-TC, STAGED NS). The eager Muon manages
300	    //    TWO param groups with INDEPENDENT hyperparameters: a 2D-matrix group
301	    //    (lr/momentum carried by the main lr/beta1 fields, consumed by the P2.7 NS
302	    //    + apply) and a 1D-weight AdamW group (muon.py:115-125: adamw_lr,
303	    //    adamw_betas, shared weight_decay). A single global scalar set cannot map
304	    //    the main lr/beta1 onto BOTH groups, so the 1D AdamW tail (P3) reads these
305	    //    aux_* fields instead. aux_bc1/bc2 are NOT carried — the muon branch
306	    //    computes them on-device (1-aux_beta^step), shrinking the mirror surface.
307	    //    Defaults mirror the eager Muon adamw_* defaults; every non-Muon caller is
308	    //    byte-identical (only the OptId::Muon P3 branch reads aux_*).
309	    float aux_lr    = 1e-3f;  // Muon 1D-group AdamW lr (eager adamw_lr)
310	    float aux_beta1 = 0.9f;   // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[0] (eager adamw_betas[0])
311	    float aux_beta2 = 0.98f;  // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[1] (eager adamw_betas[1])
312	    // ── LookSAM append-only widening (decoder/vit/mamba L3-TC, MODEL-COUPLED SAM
313	    //    2nd backward). rho = SAM perturbation radius; looksam_sam = the every-k
314	    //    SAM-step gate (1.0 ⇒ run the in-kernel perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g;
315	    //    0.0 ⇒ reuse the cached sam_dir, no 2nd pass). α rides the existing `alpha`
316	    //    field. Defaults are inert (rho=0 / looksam_sam=0), so every non-LookSAM
317	    //    caller is byte-identical (only OptId::LookSAM's model phase reads them).
318	    float rho         = 0.0f;
319	    float looksam_sam = 0.0f;
320	    // ── SuperGrok11/15 append-only widening (decoder/vit L3-TC, meta-net mu). The
321	    //    ONLY SG scalar that flows through here: the SharpnessMetaNet rescale (mu =
322	    //    rescale·phi(g, sharpness), supergrok11_sm90.cuh:130 / supergrok15_sm90.cuh:98).
323	    //    The phi WEIGHTS + sharpness are DEVICE pointers the cell binds directly (not
324	    //    scalars). rho is SHARED with LookSAM (SG's SAM perturbation radius also rides
325	    //    st.rho); st.alpha carries the SG meta-net strength (the apply tail reads it).
326	    //    Inert default (0.0 ⇒ mu=0 ⇒ the SG tail degenerates to AdamW on g) for every
327	    //    non-SG caller; layout stays byte-identical (only the SG P2.45 phase + tail read it).
328	    float sg_rescale  = 0.0f;
329	    // ── SuperGrok11 append-only widening (decoder/vit/mamba L3-TC, per-tensor cosine
330	    //    gate). gate_temp = the SharpnessMetaNet gate_temperature; the P2.45 cosine
331	    //    finalizer computes gate = sigmoid(gate_temp · cos(grad, mu)) (sg11_finalize_
332	    //    gate, algorithms/supergrok11.h). KEEP IN LOCK-STEP with the dispatch.cpp +
333	    //    gfx942 FusedScalars mirrors (one trailing field). Inert default 1.0f for
334	    //    every non-SG11 caller (SG15's gate is the host st.gate scalar; this is unread).
335	    float gate_temp   = 1.0f;
336	};

338	// Fold the runtime scalars into a FusedOptState (pointers are bound separately
339	// by each cell). Single seam so every cell applies the SAME scalar mapping — no
340	// per-cell drift in which field a scalar lands in. apply_optimizer<> reads these
341	// exact fields, so this is the bridge that un-freezes bc1/bc2/gate/d_factor/etc.
342	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ void apply_scalars(FusedOptState& st,
343	                                                        const FusedScalars& s) {
344	    st.lr           = s.lr;
345	    st.beta1        = s.beta1;
346	    st.beta2        = s.beta2;
347	    st.eps          = s.eps;
348	    st.wd           = s.wd;
349	    st.bc1          = s.bc1;
350	    st.bc2          = s.bc2;
351	    st.alpha        = s.alpha;
352	    st.beta         = s.beta;
353	    st.lamb         = s.lamb;
354	    st.alpha_max    = s.alpha_max;
355	    st.gate         = s.gate;
356	    st.d_factor     = s.d_factor;
357	    st.neg_lr_scale = s.neg_lr_scale;
358	    st.decay_factor = s.decay_factor;
359	    st.gamma        = s.gamma;       // GrokAdamW layer-wise β1 decay rate
360	    st.grad_clip    = s.grad_clip;   // GrokAdamW global grad-norm clip threshold
361	    // st.clip_coef is NOT host-bound: the kernel computes it on-device (P2.5) from
362	    // the reduced grad's global L2 norm and st.grad_clip, then applies it in P3.
363	    st.d0           = s.d0;          // Prodigy d0 (step-1 d_prev cold-start)
364	    st.d_coef       = s.d_coef;      // Prodigy candidate-d scale
365	    st.beta3        = s.beta3;       // Prodigy EMA decay (sqrt(beta2))
366	    st.aux_lr       = s.aux_lr;      // Muon 1D-group AdamW lr (eager adamw_lr)
367	    st.aux_beta1    = s.aux_beta1;   // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[0]
368	    st.aux_beta2    = s.aux_beta2;   // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[1]
369	    st.rho          = s.rho;         // LookSAM / SuperGrok11/15 SAM perturbation radius
370	    st.looksam_sam  = s.looksam_sam; // LookSAM every-k SAM-step gate (1=run 2nd bwd)
371	    st.sg_rescale   = s.sg_rescale;  // SuperGrok11/15 SharpnessMetaNet rescale (mu=rescale·phi)
372	    st.gate_temp    = s.gate_temp;   // SuperGrok11 cosine-gate temperature (sigmoid(gate_temp·cos))
373	    // st.d_factor is NOT host-bound for the STAGED-d cell: the kernel's Prodigy
374	    // reduction stage computes it on-device (between B2 and P3) and stashes it.
375	    // st.param_init / st.prodigy_persist are device pointers bound by the cell.
376	}

378	// Dispatch to the REAL per-element optimizer step. Each branch is a genuine,
379	// distinct call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h — there is no AdamW fallback.
380	template <OptId Opt>
381	__device__ __forceinline__ void apply_optimizer(
382	        float* __restrict__ params, const float* __restrict__ grad,
383	        int64_t idx, int step, const FusedOptState& st) {
384	    (void)step;  // referenced only by the cold-start branches (grokfast/grokadamw)
385	    if constexpr (Opt == OptId::AdamW) {
386	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
387	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad,
388	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
389	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Lion) {
390	        algo::lion_step<float, float>(
391	            params, st.exp_avg, grad, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.wd, idx);
392	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Grokfast) {
393	        // COLD-START (state-aware tail; owner baseline blocker (a)): the eager
394	        // Grokfast seeds the slow-grad EMA with the FIRST gradient, not zeros
395	        // (grokfast.py _group_cache: state["ema"] = grad0.clone()), because a
396	        // zero seed under-amplifies the early grokking phase and the kernel
397	        // applies no EMA bias correction. The persistent [m|v|extra] state cache
398	        // zero-inits ema=0, so at step 1 we must seed ema=grad HERE — then
399	        // grokfast_fused_step's e_new = alpha*g + (1-alpha)*g = g matches the
400	        // eager ema=grad0 exactly. Per-element on this thread's own idx (the P3
401	        // tail owns each element once), so no race / no barrier needed. For
402	        // step>1 the cache carries the real EMA forward (no reseed).
403	        if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];
404	        algo::grokfast_fused_step<float, float>(
405	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.ema, grad,
406	            st.alpha, st.lamb, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
407	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
408	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::GrokAdamW) {
409	        // FAITHFUL GrokAdamW (decoder L3-TC conversion) — all THREE eager
410	        // mechanisms now land, so the cell is no longer a hollow pass:
411	        //
412	        //  (i)  PER-TENSOR LAYER-WISE β1 = β1·(1-γ)^layer (grokadamw.py
413	        //       _layer_beta1_by_id). The caller (the P3 work-steal loop, which
414	        //       owns the tensor index t == the flat named_parameters() layer
415	        //       index) has ALREADY rebased st.beta1 to β1_i AND st.bc1 to
416	        //       1-β1_i^step for THIS tensor before calling us (see the
417	        //       fused_decoder_megakernel P3 block, guarded by if constexpr
418	        //       GrokAdamW). So st.beta1/st.bc1 here are the per-tensor values;
419	        //       this branch just consumes them. bc2 stays global (β2 is not
420	        //       layer-wise). This is the mechanism that fails the STATE gate at
421	        //       step 1 if dropped (m-rel 0.895), so it is load-bearing.
422	        //
423	        //  (ii) GLOBAL GRAD-NORM CLIP to grad_clip (bindings.cpp
424	        //       clip_grad_norms_device_side → a GLOBAL norm over ALL tensors,
425	        //       one scalar clip_coef = grad_clip/(‖g‖₂+1e-6) applied to every
426	        //       grad when ‖g‖₂ > grad_clip). The kernel computes ‖g‖₂ + clip_coef
427	        //       ON-DEVICE in P2.5 (deterministic ascending-CTA reduction over the
428	        //       reduced grad) and stashes st.clip_coef; we scale the grad by it
429	        //       HERE. Eager clips IN-PLACE before the ema-seed AND the step, so we
430	        //       use the SAME clipped grad for both. At step 1 ‖g‖₂≈0.72<1 ⇒
431	        //       clip_coef=1 (inert), but it FIRES multi-step — the missing-clip
432	        //       2e-4 divergence is what the multi-step parity check catches.
433	        //
434	        //  (iii) ADAPTIVE α = alpha_init·exp(-κ·signal): in-context this is a
435	        //       genuine NO-OP. No race/gate path feeds (train_loss, val_loss) to
436	        //       GrokAdamW.step(), so eager α stays at alpha_init for ALL steps =
437	        //       the static st.alpha bound here. Faithful, not dropped (verified:
438	        //       fused_train_step/fused_optimizer_step/race never pass losses).
439	        //
440	        // COLD-START: eager seeds ema = the UNCLIPPED grad0, NOT the clipped grad.
441	        // grokadamw.py _group_cache clones state["ema"] = p.grad.clone() (the raw
442	        // gradient) BEFORE grokadamw_fused_step's in-place clip_grad_norms_device_
443	        // side (bindings.cpp:215) runs — so the cold-start seed is the UNCLIPPED
444	        // grad while the EMA filter input + amplification use the CLIPPED grad. The
445	        // prior `st.ema[idx]=gc` seeded the CLIPPED grad, which is byte-identical
446	        // when the clip is INERT (clip_coef==1 ⇒ gc==grad) — every currently-green
447	        // config — but diverges the m/ema state when the clip FIRES (the forced-fire
448	        // multi-step parity surfaced this: kernel ema/clipped==1.0 vs eager 1/coef).
449	        // Fix: seed the UNCLIPPED grad; keep the filter + g_amp on gc.
450	        const float gc = grad[idx] * st.clip_coef;   // (ii) global-clipped grad
451	        if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];       // cold-start on UNCLIPPED grad
452	        // EMA filter + amplification (csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h math), on gc.
453	        const float ema_new = st.alpha * st.ema[idx] + (1.0f - st.alpha) * gc;
454	        st.ema[idx] = ema_new;
455	        const float g_amp = gc + st.lamb * ema_new;
456	        // Adam moments + decoupled-WD apply: the canonical grokadamw_adam_tail
457	        // (bit-identical to grokadamw_step's tail), driven by the per-tensor
458	        // st.beta1/st.bc1 (i) and the un-inverted global st.bc2.
459	        float m_out, v_out, p_out;
460	        algo::grokadamw_adam_tail(
461	            g_amp, params[idx], st.exp_avg[idx], st.exp_avg_sq[idx],
462	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2,
463	            m_out, v_out, p_out);
464	        st.exp_avg[idx]    = m_out;
465	        st.exp_avg_sq[idx] = v_out;
466	        params[idx]        = p_out;
467	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::LookSAM) {
468	        algo::looksam_apply_step<float, float>(
469	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.sam_dir, grad,
470	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
471	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
472	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Prodigy) {
473	        algo::prodigy_apply_step<float, float>(
474	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.s_track, grad,
475	            st.d_factor, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
476	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
477	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::NeuralGrok) {
478	        // psi_b2 is the scalar packed immediately after psi_W2 in the `extra`
479	        // buffer (extra[kPsiB2Off] == st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]). Read it ON-DEVICE
480	        // here, where the pointer is dereferenceable — the host cell cannot
481	        // deref a device pointer, so it leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default.
482	        // This threads the real psi_b2 bias (previously stuck at 0.0).
483	        const float psi_b2 = (st.psi_W2 != nullptr) ? st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]
484	                                                     : st.psi_b2;
485	        // GLOBAL grad-norm clip (eager neuralgrok clips grad IN-PLACE via
486	        // clip_grad_norms_device_side BEFORE psi+amp). st.clip_coef is computed in the
487	        // megakernel's P2.5 (extended to NeuralGrok); 1.0 when grad_clip<=0 or norm<=clip.
488	        // psi reads |clipped grad|; the apply scales grad by the same coef internally.
489	        const float gc = grad[idx] * st.clip_coef;
490	        const float psi = algo::neuralgrok_psi_forward<kPsiHidden>(
491	            fabsf(gc), st.psi_W1, st.psi_b1, st.psi_W2, psi_b2);
492	        algo::neuralgrok_apply_step<float, float>(
493	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, psi,
494	            st.alpha, st.beta, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
495	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx, st.clip_coef);
496	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Muon) {
497	        // 2D params: NS-orthogonalized direction precomputed; tail is the
498	        // momentum-decayed scaled apply. (1D params use AdamW upstream.)
499	        algo::muon_update_step<float>(
500	            params, st.orth, st.neg_lr_scale, st.decay_factor, idx);
501	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok11) {
502	        algo::sg11_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
503	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
504	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
505	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
506	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok15) {
507	        algo::sg15_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
508	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
509	            st.alpha, st.alpha_max, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
510	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
511	    } else {  // OptId::SuperGrok2 — Adam apply on the meta-net smart gradient.
512	        // The CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net (separate launch) produced st.smart_grad;
513	        // the fused tail is the real Adam apply on it (faithful to the per-op
514	        // SG2 path's apply stage).
515	        const float* g = (st.smart_grad != nullptr) ? st.smart_grad : grad;
516	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
517	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, g,
518	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
519	    }
520	}

91	//  PrecomputeWorkspace — global scratch the cross-CTA stages reduce through.
92	//
93	//  Grouped as one POD (like PersistentContext) so the codegen kernel signature
94	//  stays uniform. The host allocates each pointer the chosen optimizer needs and
95	//  zero-fills the rest (a stage touches ONLY its optimizer's buffers). All FP32.
96	//
97	//  DETERMINISM: `partials` is a per-CTA slot array (length >= ctx.n_ctas, or
98	//  2*n_ctas for the two-value prodigy reduce). Each CTA writes its OWN slot (no
99	//  contention, no atomic); after a grid barrier, one owner thread sums the slots
100	//  in ascending index order — a fixed, reproducible fp32 summation. This is the
101	//  "owner-computes tree" that REPLACES the live path's atomicAdd accumulate.
102	// =========================================================================
103	struct PrecomputeWorkspace {
104	    // Prodigy: r/s partial slots (2 per CTA: [0..n_ctas) = r, [n_ctas..) = s)
105	    // and the reduced d output (a single device scalar the apply reads via
106	    // st.d_factor). d_prev is carried in by the cell.
107	    float* prodigy_partials = nullptr;   // length >= 2 * n_ctas
108	    float* prodigy_d        = nullptr;   // length 1 (reduced d; also st.d_factor)
109	    // Muon: Newton-Schulz scratch for ONE matrix at a time (rows*cols floats
110	    // each), plus a per-CTA Frobenius-norm partial slot array.
111	    float* muon_buf  = nullptr;          // momentum buffer (rows*cols), persists
112	    float* muon_X    = nullptr;          // current iterate           (rows*cols)
113	    float* muon_A    = nullptr;          // A = X Xᵀ  (rows*rows)
114	    float* muon_AX   = nullptr;          // A X       (rows*cols)
115	    float* muon_AAX  = nullptr;          // A (A X)   (rows*cols)
116	    float* muon_orth = nullptr;          // NS output = st.orth        (rows*cols)
117	    float* muon_nrm_partials = nullptr;  // length >= n_ctas (‖buf‖_F² partials)
118	    float* muon_inv_norm     = nullptr;  // length 1 (1/(‖buf‖_F + 1e-7))
119	};

121	// =========================================================================
122	//  Deterministic cross-CTA owner-computes sum.
123	//
124	//  Each CTA (its leader thread) has already published `my_partial` into
125	//  `slots[blockIdx.x]`. After the caller's grid barrier guarantees every slot is
126	//  visible, EVERY CTA's leader recomputes the SAME total by summing slots[0..
127	//  n-1] in ascending order. Fixed order ⇒ identical fp32 result on every CTA, no
128	//  atomics. Returns the total on the leader (thread 0); other threads return 0.
129	//  Caller broadcasts within the block if all threads need it.
130	// =========================================================================
131	__device__ __forceinline__ float owner_sum_slots(const float* __restrict__ slots,
132	                                                  unsigned n) {
133	    float acc = 0.0f;
134	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
135	        // Ascending fixed-index summation — deterministic fp32 order.
136	        for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; ++i) acc += slots[i];
137	    }
138	    return acc;
139	}

190	// ============================================================================
191	// (3a) STAGED — PRODIGY: cross-ALL-tensors d-adaptation reduction.
192	//
193	// Shape: GLOBAL. r and s are sums over EVERY element of EVERY parameter tensor
194	// (one scalar d for the whole model). Semantic source — the per-op three-kernel
195	// orchestration: prodigy_reduce_kernel (prodigy_sm90.cuh:85-109) accumulates the
196	// per-element partials via prodigy_partials_step, then prodigy_update_d
197	// (prodigy.h:56-65) combines them into d. The multi-tensor live driver is
198	// launch_multi_tensor_prodigy_fused_reduce_step (prodigy_sm90.cuh:465-544).
199	//
200	// IN-KERNEL vs HOST split (faithful to the live path):
201	//   * IN-KERNEL (this stage): the per-step Σ r_local / Σ s_local over all tensors
202	//     (prodigy_partials_step, prodigy.h:28-53) + prodigy_update_d (prodigy.h:56-
203	//     65). This is the cross-tensor reduction Audit-C flagged.
204	//   * HOST / CELL (NOT in this stage — documented, not hidden): the PERSISTENT
205	//     beta3-EMA decay of (r,s) across steps and the d_coef scaling live in the
206	//     host launcher (prodigy_sm90.cuh:488-521 / bindings.cpp:1246-1264), outside
207	//     prodigy.h. The grokking race uses that EMA estimator. The in-kernel stage
208	//     here computes the INSTANTANEOUS Σ-partials + max() update (d0=1e-6 init);
209	//     a cell wanting the EMA form decays prodigy_partials in the workspace
210	//     before the barrier and scales before prodigy_update_d — see
211	//     INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md. The DEVICE math (prodigy.h) is byte-unchanged.
212	//
213	// DETERMINISM: REPLACES prodigy_sm90.cuh's atomicAdd (:105-108,:135-138) with
214	//   per-CTA (r,s) slot publish → grid barrier → owner-computes fixed-order sum →
215	//   prodigy_update_d. No float atomic.
216	//
217	// TWO-PHASE STAGE (the caller drives the barrier between them so the codegen owns
218	// the grid sync, consistent with fused_megakernel.cuh's phase pipeline):
219	//   Phase A: each CTA drains the task queue, accumulates this CTA's (r,s) over
220	//            its claimed tensors, publishes to ws.prodigy_partials slots.
221	//   [caller grid barrier — every slot visible]
222	//   Phase B: every CTA owner-sums the slots in fixed order and writes d to
223	//            ws.prodigy_d (== st.d_factor for the apply tail).
224	// ============================================================================
225	
226	// Phase A — accumulate this CTA's (r,s) partial over all its queued tensors and
227	// publish to the per-CTA slots. `param_init` is the Prodigy trajectory anchor
228	// (one flat blob parallel to params). Drains the SAME task queue the apply uses.
229	__device__ inline void prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseA(
230	        const PersistentContext& ctx,
231	        const float* __restrict__ params,
232	        const float* __restrict__ param_init,
233	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
234	        const int* __restrict__ sizes, const int* __restrict__ offsets,
235	        float d_prev,
236	        PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
237	    __shared__ int task_slot;
238	    float r_acc = 0.0f, s_acc = 0.0f;
239	    TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
240	    for (int t = q.next_block(&task_slot); t < ctx.n_tasks;
241	         t = q.next_block(&task_slot)) {
242	        const int n = sizes[t];
243	        const int64_t off = (int64_t)offsets[t];
244	        for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) {
245	            // Canonical per-element partials (prodigy.h:28-53). r/s carry d² so
246	            // d_hat=r/s is scale-free; s is the L1 norm Σ d²·|g|.
247	            float r_one = 0.0f, s_one = 0.0f;
248	            algo::prodigy_partials_step(params + off, param_init + off, grad + off,
249	                                        d_prev, (int64_t)i, r_one, s_one);
250	            r_acc += r_one;
251	            s_acc += s_one;
252	        }
253	    }
254	    // Deterministic in-CTA reduction of this CTA's (r,s) — fixed thread count.
255	    float r_block, s_block;
256	    prim::block_reduce_sum2_f32(r_acc, s_acc, r_block, s_block);
257	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
258	        // Per-CTA slot publish (no atomic). r slots [0..n_ctas), s slots after.
259	        ws.prodigy_partials[blockIdx.x]              = r_block;
260	        ws.prodigy_partials[ctx.n_ctas + blockIdx.x] = s_block;
261	    }
262	}
263	
264	// Phase B — owner-computes deterministic sum of all CTA slots, then the canonical
265	// d update. Runs AFTER the caller's grid barrier. Every CTA writes the same d
266	// (redundant but race-free); the apply reads ws.prodigy_d via st.d_factor.
267	__device__ inline void prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseB(
268	        const PersistentContext& ctx, float d_prev, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
269	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
270	        // Fixed-order sums (ascending CTA index) — deterministic fp32.
271	        float r_sum = 0.0f, s_sum = 0.0f;
272	        for (unsigned c = 0; c < ctx.n_ctas; ++c) {
273	            r_sum += ws.prodigy_partials[c];
274	            s_sum += ws.prodigy_partials[ctx.n_ctas + c];
275	        }
276	        // Canonical d update (prodigy.h:56-65): d = max(d_prev, r/|s|).
277	        ws.prodigy_d[0] = algo::prodigy_update_d(d_prev, r_sum, s_sum);
278	    }
279	}

282	// (3b) STAGED — MUON: momentum update + Newton-Schulz orthogonalization.
283	//
284	// Shape: per-MATRIX, GRID-COOPERATIVE. A matmul is cross-element (X Xᵀ couples
285	// every row), and a realistic 2D weight does not fit one CTA's SMEM — so muon's
286	// precompute CANNOT follow the one-CTA-per-tensor element-wise model. All CTAs
287	// cooperate on ONE matrix at a time, with a grid barrier between each matmul and
288	// between NS iterations; the caller loops matrices.
289	//
290	// Semantic source — bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step (bindings.cpp:930-1014):
291	//   buf = momentum*buf + grad                    (bindings.cpp:948)
292	//   inv_norm = 1/(‖buf‖_F + 1e-7)                (bindings.cpp:962-963)
293	//   X = buf*inv_norm                             (bindings.cpp:964)
294	//   repeat ns_steps (default 5):                 (bindings.cpp:991-1007)
295	//       A   = X Xᵀ                               (bindings.cpp:992, torch::mm)
296	//       AX  = A X                                 (bindings.cpp:993)
297	//       AAX = A AX                                (bindings.cpp:994)
298	//       Y = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX  (a,b,c = 3.4445,-4.7750,2.0315; :938-940)
299	//   orth = final Y
300	//   scale = 0.2*sqrt(max(rows,cols)); neg_lr_scale=-lr*scale; decay=1-lr*wd
301	//                                                (bindings.cpp:980-983)
302	// Per-element bodies are CALLED from muon.h: muon_momentum_normalize_step
303	// (muon.h:33-46), muon_ns_combine_step (muon.h:49-60). The MATMULS are NEW
304	// device code: the live path delegates X Xᵀ etc. to torch::mm/cuBLAS
305	// (bindings.cpp:992-994), NOT a per-element canonical fn — so a tiled owner-
306	// computes matmul is legitimate and is cited to that mm sequence. The drift
307	// guard requires only that the ELEMENTWISE pieces call muon.h, which they do.
308	//
309	// DETERMINISM: the matmul is an owner-computes inner product per output element
310	// (one thread sums the k-dimension in ascending order — fixed fp32 order, no
311	// atomic). ‖buf‖_F² uses per-CTA slot publish → barrier → owner_sum (same as
312	// prodigy). 1D params are NOT handled here (they take the AdamW tail upstream,
313	// muon.h:75-76 / bindings.cpp:970-977).
314	//
315	// STAGE STRUCTURE (caller drives every grid barrier — one matrix per call):
316	//   muon_momentum_norm_phaseA → [barrier] → muon_norm_reduce_phaseB (writes
317	//     inv_norm) → [barrier] → muon_scale_X (X = buf*inv_norm)
318	//   then ns_steps × { muon_matmul A=XXᵀ → [barrier] → muon_matmul AX=A·X →
319	//     [barrier] → muon_matmul AAX=A·AX → [barrier] → muon_ns_combine_phase
320	//     (orth = a·X + b·AX + c·AAX) → [barrier] → swap(X, orth) }
321	//   The caller then binds st.orth=<final NS buffer>, st.neg_lr_scale,
322	//   st.decay_factor and runs apply_optimizer<Muon> (muon.h:63-73). The exact
323	//   barrier/swap sequence + stride args are in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md §3.
324	// ============================================================================
325	
326	static constexpr float kMuonNS_A = 3.4445f;   // bindings.cpp:938
327	static constexpr float kMuonNS_B = -4.7750f;  // bindings.cpp:939
328	static constexpr float kMuonNS_C = 2.0315f;   // bindings.cpp:940
329	static constexpr float kMuonNormEps = 1e-7f;  // bindings.cpp:962
330	
331	// momentum update Phase A: buf = momentum*buf + grad, accumulate ‖buf‖_F²
332	// partial per CTA. (We compute the norm from buf here, then scale X after the
333	// reduction — equivalent to bindings.cpp:948,962-964; we cannot scale X yet
334	// because inv_norm needs the full-matrix norm.) All CTAs cooperate over the
335	// flat [rows*cols] matrix via a grid-stride loop.
336	__device__ inline void muon_momentum_norm_phaseA(
337	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
338	        int64_t numel, float momentum,
339	        PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
340	    float nrm2 = 0.0f;
341	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
342	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
343	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
344	        // buf = momentum*buf + grad (plain SGD-momentum, muon.h:43-44 body).
345	        const float b = momentum * ws.muon_buf[i] + grad[i];
346	        ws.muon_buf[i] = b;
347	        nrm2 += b * b;
348	    }
349	    float blk = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(nrm2);
350	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) ws.muon_nrm_partials[blockIdx.x] = blk;
351	}
352	
353	// momentum norm Phase B (after grid barrier): owner-sum the per-CTA ‖buf‖_F²
354	// slots in fixed order, write inv_norm = 1/(sqrt(Σ) + 1e-7) (bindings.cpp:962-
355	// 963). The X = buf*inv_norm assignment is split off into muon_scale_X (below):
356	// the canonical muon_momentum_normalize_step (muon.h:33-46) does buf-update AND
357	// X-scale in one shot, but we need the FULL-MATRIX norm before we can scale, so
358	// phaseA folded grad into buf (the muon.h:43 body) and this reduction yields
359	// inv_norm — the X=buf*inv_norm step (a single multiply, bindings.cpp:964, NOT
360	// orthogonalization math) then runs post-barrier so every CTA sees the published
361	// norm. The orthogonalization MATH (the NS combine) stays on the canonical fn.
362	__device__ inline void muon_norm_reduce_phaseB(
363	        const PersistentContext& ctx, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
364	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
365	        float s = 0.0f;
366	        for (unsigned c = 0; c < ctx.n_ctas; ++c) s += ws.muon_nrm_partials[c];
367	        ws.muon_inv_norm[0] = 1.0f / (sqrtf(s) + kMuonNormEps);
368	    }
369	}
370	
371	// X = buf * inv_norm (bindings.cpp:964). Single multiply (not optimizer math);
372	// runs after the barrier that publishes inv_norm. All CTAs grid-stride the flat
373	// matrix.
374	__device__ inline void muon_scale_X(int64_t numel, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
375	    const float inv_norm = ws.muon_inv_norm[0];
376	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
377	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
378	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
379	        ws.muon_X[i] = ws.muon_buf[i] * inv_norm;
380	    }
381	}
382	
383	// Owner-computes tiled matmul C[m,n] = sum_k A[m,k] * B[k,n], grid-cooperative
384	// over the OUTPUT elements (one thread owns one output and sums the contraction
385	// in ASCENDING k — deterministic fp32, no atomic). `bT` selects B vs Bᵀ so we
386	// can express X Xᵀ (A=X[r,c], B=X[r,c] with bT → contract over c giving [r,r])
387	// and A X (contract over r) with one helper. Row-major [rows*cols] layout
388	// matching the flat workspace buffers.
389	//   - For A = X Xᵀ:  out[r1,r2] = Σ_c X[r1,c] X[r2,c]   (M=rows,N=rows,K=cols)
390	//   - For AX = A X:   out[r,c]   = Σ_j A[r,j] X[j,c]     (M=rows,N=cols,K=rows)
391	__device__ inline void muon_matmul(
392	        const float* __restrict__ A, const float* __restrict__ B,
393	        float* __restrict__ C, int M, int N, int K,
394	        int A_rowstride, int B_rowstride,
395	        bool b_transposed) {
396	    const int64_t total = (int64_t)M * N;
397	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
398	    for (int64_t idx = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
399	         idx < total; idx += gstride) {
400	        const int row = (int)(idx / N);
401	        const int col = (int)(idx % N);
402	        float acc = 0.0f;
403	        const float* arow = A + (int64_t)row * A_rowstride;
404	        if (b_transposed) {
405	            // B[col, k] (row `col` of B, length K). Used for X Xᵀ.
406	            const float* brow = B + (int64_t)col * B_rowstride;
407	            for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) acc += arow[k] * brow[k];
408	        } else {
409	            // B[k, col]. Used for A X.
410	            for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) acc += arow[k] * B[(int64_t)k * B_rowstride + col];
411	        }
412	        C[idx] = acc;
413	    }
414	}

416	// One Newton-Schulz iteration body's polynomial combine over the flat matrix:
417	// X_next = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX (muon.h:49-60, called per element). The matmuls
418	// A/AX/AAX must already be computed (by muon_matmul, with caller barriers
419	// between them). Writes into ws.muon_X in place is unsafe (combine reads X), so
420	// we combine into ws.muon_orth then the caller swaps orth↔X for the next iter,
421	// or — on the LAST iter — leaves the result in ws.muon_orth as the final
422	// orthogonalized direction.
423	__device__ inline void muon_ns_combine_phase(int64_t numel,
424	                                             PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
425	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
426	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
427	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
428	        // Canonical combine body (muon.h:49-60): Y = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX.
429	        algo::muon_ns_combine_step(ws.muon_orth, ws.muon_X, ws.muon_AX,
430	                                   ws.muon_AAX, kMuonNS_A, kMuonNS_B, kMuonNS_C,
431	                                   i);
432	    }
433	}

436	// (3c) STAGED — SUPERGROK11: meta-MLP mu (per element) + per-TENSOR cosine gate.
437	//
438	// Semantic source — supergrok11_fused_step (bindings.cpp:1339-1418) +
439	// sg11_mu_metanet_kernel (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:112-134) +
440	// compute_cosine_gate_fused (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:275-286).
441	//
442	// The live path does (bindings.cpp:1407-1416):
443	//   1. mu = rescale * phi(grad, sharpness)  with smart_grad = grad + 0*mu = grad
444	//      (mu_metanet called with alpha=0, so smart_grad == grad — the gate's first
445	//      argument IS grad).                          (bindings.cpp:1407-1409)

447	//      compute_cosine_gate_fused → sg11_finalize_gate, supergrok11_sm90.cuh).

524	        float* __restrict__ mu_blob,
525	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
526	        const float* __restrict__ sharpness,
527	        const float* __restrict__ momentum,
528	        const float* sW1, const float* sb1, const float* sW2,
529	        float b2, float rescale,

533	    // Sweep A): for each element it writes mu_out[gi]=rescale·phi(g,sharpness) and

27	// Per-element contribution to r and s partial sums.
28	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
29	__device__ __forceinline__ void prodigy_partials_step(
30	    const ParamT* __restrict__ param,
31	    const ParamT* __restrict__ param_init,
32	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
33	    const float d_prev,
34	    const int64_t idx,
35	    float& r_local,
36	    float& s_local
37	) {

39	    const float pi = static_cast<float>(param_init[idx]);
40	    const float g  = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
41	
42	    // Numerator and denominator must carry the SAME power of d so the estimate
43	    // d_hat = r/s is scale-free (degree 0 in d). The denominator carries d²
44	    // (below), so the numerator carries d² too. A degree-1 numerator (a single
45	    // d_prev) made d_hat ∝ 1/d, which at the d0 = 1e-6 init blew d up by ~1e6×
46	    // in a single step (catapult) and destroyed training — the fused kernel
47	    // matched the canonical paper formula's intent only once both sides are d².
48	    r_local += g * (pi - p) * d_prev * d_prev;
49	    // Prodigy d-estimate denominator is the L1 norm ||s||_1 = Σ_j |d²·g_j|
50	    // (arxiv 2306.06101), so accumulate |g| per coordinate. (Previously this
51	    // summed signed g and took |Σ| at reduce time — abs-of-sum ≠ L1 norm.)

10	// Same structure as v1.5 but the gating SIGNAL is the cosine between grad
11	// and momentum (computed per-parameter), not a sigmoid of training accuracy.
12	// The gate is the SIGMOID of that cosine signal scaled by gate_temperature —
13	// what distinguishes SG11 from SG15 is WHICH quantity feeds the sigmoid (the
14	// per-parameter cosine here vs. SG15's training-accuracy scalar), not the
15	// final squashing function.
16	//
17	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
18	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
19	//
20	// Pipeline per step (two cooperative sweeps):
21	//
22	//   Sweep A — meta-net forward:
23	//     mu = mlp_phi(grad, sharpness)
24	//     gate_num += grad * momentum
25	//     gate_den_g += grad * grad
26	//     gate_den_m += momentum * momentum
27	//
28	//   Sweep B — apply:
29	//     cos  = gate_num / sqrt(gate_den_g * gate_den_m + eps)   // cos_sim(grad, momentum)
30	//     gate = sigmoid(gate_temperature * cos)                  // see sg11_finalize_gate
31	//     smart_grad = grad + (1 - gate) * alpha * mu
32	//     AdamW step on smart_grad with trust-ratio scaling.

39	// MLP forward: GELU hidden, linear output (matches the canonical trainable
40	// PyTorch SharpnessMetaNet, which uses nn.GELU). Phi weights: W1[H,2], b1[H],
41	// W2[H], b2.
42	template <int H>
43	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg11_phi_forward(
44	    const float grad_val,
45	    const float sharp_val,
46	    const float* __restrict__ W1,
47	    const float* __restrict__ b1,
48	    const float* __restrict__ W2,
49	    const float b2
50	) {
51	    float h_acc = 0.0f;
52	    #pragma unroll
53	    for (int j = 0; j < H; j++) {
54	        float h = W1[j * 2] * grad_val + W1[j * 2 + 1] * sharp_val + b1[j];
55	        // Exact erf GELU — matches torch.nn.GELU() in the trainable meta-net.
56	        h = 0.5f * h * (1.0f + erff(h * 0.70710678118654752f));
57	        h_acc += W2[j] * h;
58	    }
59	    return h_acc + b2;
60	}

62	// CANONICAL gate finalization (THE single source). Turns the three pre-reduced
63	// cosine accumulators into the scalar gate the apply tail consumes:
64	//   cos  = gate_num / sqrt(gate_den_g * gate_den_m + eps)   // cos_sim(grad, momentum)
65	//   gate = sigmoid(gate_temp * cos) = 1 / (1 + exp(-gate_temp * cos))
66	// The cosine SIGNAL is what makes SG11 distinct from SG15 (which feeds training
67	// accuracy into its sigmoid); only the FINAL squashing is a sigmoid here, using
68	// the plumbed gate_temperature (NOT a bare clamp — the historical impl clamped
69	// the raw cosine and ignored the temperature). Both CUDA consumers (the per-op
70	// compute_cosine_gate_fused and the L3-TC sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor)
71	// derive from THIS; the Python/Pallas/test references mirror the same expression.
72	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ float sg11_finalize_gate(
73	    const float gate_num,
74	    const float gate_den_g,
75	    const float gate_den_m,
76	    const float gate_temp,
77	    const float eps = 1e-12f
78	) {
79	    const float denom = sqrtf(gate_den_g * gate_den_m + eps);
80	    const float cos_sim = (denom > 0.0f) ? (gate_num / denom) : 0.0f;
81	    // expf (NOT the device-only __expf) so this single source compiles on the
82	    // HOST consumer (compute_cosine_gate_fused) and the DEVICE consumer alike.
83	    return 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-gate_temp * cos_sim));
84	}

90	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
91	    const float* __restrict__ sharpness,
92	    const float* __restrict__ momentum,
93	    const float mu_val,

96	    float& gate_den_g_local,
97	    float& gate_den_m_local
98	) {

102	    gate_num_local   += g * m;
103	    gate_den_g_local += g * g;
104	    gate_den_m_local += m * m;

108	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
109	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg11_sweep_b_step(
110	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
111	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
112	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
113	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
114	    const float* __restrict__ mu,
115	    const float gate,            // pre-reduced gate = sigmoid(gate_temp * cos_sim)
116	    const float alpha,           // meta-net strength
117	    const float lr,
118	    const float beta1,
119	    const float beta2,
120	    const float eps,
121	    const float wd,
122	    const float bc1,
123	    const float bc2,
124	    const int64_t idx
125	) {
126	    const float g  = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
127	    const float p  = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
128	    const float u  = mu[idx];
129	
130	    const float smart_grad = g + (1.0f - gate) * alpha * u;
131	
132	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * smart_grad;
133	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * smart_grad * smart_grad;
134	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
135	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;

137	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
138	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
139	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));

4	// Reference: Lee et al. 2024, "Grokfast: Accelerated Grokking by
5	// Amplifying Slow Gradients" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20233),
6	// EMA-amplified gradient form.
7	//
8	// Simplest grokking-aware AdamW: EMA filter + amplification, then standard
9	// Adam. Two operational modes:
10	//
11	//   (A) ema-only:   ema = alpha * ema + (1-alpha) * g;
12	//                   grad_out = g + lamb * ema       (consumed by downstream Adam)
13	//
14	//   (B) fused:      same EMA update, then immediately run Adam on g_amp.
15	//
16	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
17	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.

24	// EMA-only path: update EMA and write amplified gradient back into grad_out.
25	template <typename GradT>
26	__device__ __forceinline__ void grokfast_ema_step(
27	    float* __restrict__ ema,
28	    GradT* __restrict__ grad_out,
29	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad_in,
30	    const float alpha,
31	    const float lamb,
32	    const int64_t idx
33	) {

35	    const float e = alpha * ema[idx] + (1.0f - alpha) * g;
36	    ema[idx] = e;
37	    grad_out[idx] = static_cast<GradT>(g + lamb * e);
38	}

40	// Fully fused: EMA + amplification + AdamW in a single per-element step.
41	// Keeps the amplified gradient in registers from compute through Adam.
42	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
43	__device__ __forceinline__ void grokfast_fused_step(
44	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
45	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
46	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
47	    float* __restrict__ ema,
48	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
49	    const float grokfast_alpha,

51	    const float lr,
52	    const float beta1,
53	    const float beta2,
54	    const float eps,
55	    const float wd,
56	    const float bc1,
57	    const float bc2,

6	// persistent directions (the slow-changing components of the gradient
7	// signal).
8	//
9	// Math (decoupled weight decay variant; bias correction via division):
10	//   ema_t = alpha * ema_{t-1} + (1 - alpha) * g
11	//   g_amp = g + lamb * ema_t
12	//   m_t   = beta1 * m_{t-1} + (1 - beta1) * g_amp
13	//   v_t   = beta2 * v_{t-1} + (1 - beta2) * g_amp^2
14	//   m_hat = m_t / (1 - beta1^t)
15	//   v_hat = v_t / (1 - beta2^t)
16	//   p    -= lr * (m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps) + wd * p)
17	//
18	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
19	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.

26	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
27	__device__ __forceinline__ void grokadamw_step(
28	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
29	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
30	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
31	    float* __restrict__ ema,
32	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
33	    const float alpha,    // EMA decay (e.g. 0.98)
34	    const float lamb,     // amplification factor (e.g. 5.0)
35	    const float lr,
36	    const float beta1,
37	    const float beta2,
38	    const float eps,
39	    const float wd,
40	    const float bc1,
41	    const float bc2,
42	    const int64_t idx
43	) {
44	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
45	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
46	
47	    // EMA filter
48	    const float ema_new = alpha * ema[idx] + (1.0f - alpha) * g;
49	    ema[idx] = ema_new;
50	
51	    // Amplified gradient
52	    const float g_amp = g + lamb * ema_new;
53	
54	    // Adam moments
55	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_amp;
56	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp;
57	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
58	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
59	
60	    // Bias-corrected update with decoupled weight decay.
61	    // bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t), so divide.
62	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);

86	    const float beta2,

3	//
4	// Reference: Liu et al. 2022, "Towards Efficient and Scalable Sharpness-
5	// Aware Minimization" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02714), Algorithm 1
6	// (periodic-perturbation variant — SAM gradient is recomputed every k
7	// steps, then reused as a cached direction for intervening steps).
8	//
9	// AdamW with periodic Sharpness-Aware Minimization (every k steps).
10	//
11	// Four operations:
12	//   (1) perturb:           p_pert = p + rho * (g / ||g||)
13	//   (2) restore:           p = p_pert - rho * (g / ||g||)
14	//   (3) direction adjust:  on SAM step,    sam_dir = g_sam - g
15	//                          on normal step, g_adj   = (1-alpha)*g + alpha*sam_dir
16	//   (4) standard AdamW update with g_adj.
17	//
18	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
19	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
20	
21	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
22	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
23	
24	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
25	
26	// Step (1) — perturb in gradient direction by rho / ||g||.
27	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
28	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_perturb_step(
29	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
30	    ParamT* __restrict__ backup,
31	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
32	    const float scale,        // rho / (||g|| + eps), precomputed
33	    const int64_t idx
34	) {
35	    const ParamT p = param[idx];
36	    backup[idx] = p;
37	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(static_cast<float>(p) + scale * static_cast<float>(grad[idx]));
38	}
39	
40	// Step (2) — restore parameters from backup.
41	template <typename ParamT>
42	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_restore_step(
43	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
44	    const ParamT* __restrict__ backup,
45	    const int64_t idx
46	) {
47	    param[idx] = backup[idx];
48	}
49	
50	// Step (3) on SAM step: cache the gradient difference.
51	template <typename GradT>
52	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_set_direction(
53	    float* __restrict__ sam_dir,
54	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad_sam,
55	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad_orig,
56	    const int64_t idx
57	) {
58	    sam_dir[idx] = static_cast<float>(grad_sam[idx]) - static_cast<float>(grad_orig[idx]);
59	}
60	
61	// Step (3) on normal step + Step (4): blend cached SAM direction and run Adam.
62	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
63	__device__ __forceinline__ void looksam_apply_step(
64	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
65	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
66	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
67	    const float* __restrict__ sam_dir,
68	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
69	    const float alpha,         // SAM blend strength
70	    const float lr,
71	    const float beta1,
72	    const float beta2,
73	    const float eps,
74	    const float wd,
75	    const float bc1,
76	    const float bc2,
77	    const int64_t idx
78	) {
79	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]);
80	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
81	    const float g_adj = (1.0f - alpha) * g + alpha * sam_dir[idx];
82	
83	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_adj;
84	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_adj * g_adj;
85	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
86	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
87	
88	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
89	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
90	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
91	}
92	
93	}} // namespace sg::algorithms

1	#pragma once
2	// NeuralGrok — vendor-neutral algorithm header.
3	//
4	// Reference: Wang et al. 2024, "NeuralGrok: Accelerating Grokking via
5	// Learned Gradient Amplification" — Adam with a learned per-element
6	// amplifier (psi-net).
7	//
8	// The amplifier is a 2-layer MLP that takes |grad| as input and outputs
9	// a multiplicative scale.
10	//
11	// Two-stage compute:
12	//   (1) psi_net forward:  s = mlp(|g|)  (per-element scaling factor)
13	//   (2) apply:            g_amp = (s * alpha + beta) * g
14	//                         AdamW step on g_amp
15	//
16	// Calling convention: bc1, bc2 are passed un-inverted —
17	//   bc1 = 1 - beta1^t,  bc2 = 1 - beta2^t.
18	//
19	// The MLP weights live in constant memory on CUDA / LDS on HIP. The math
20	// here is the per-element body; the matmul is handled by the backend.
21	
22	#include "csrc/common/types.h"
23	#include "csrc/common/utils.cuh"
24	
25	namespace sg { namespace algorithms {
26	
27	// 2-layer MLP forward for a single element, with weights passed inline.
28	// W1: [H], b1: [H], W2: [H], b2: scalar.
29	// Activation: ReLU on hidden layer.
30	template <int H>
31	__device__ __forceinline__ float neuralgrok_psi_forward(
32	    const float abs_grad,
33	    const float* __restrict__ W1,
34	    const float* __restrict__ b1,
35	    const float* __restrict__ W2,
36	    const float b2
37	) {
38	    float h_acc = 0.0f;
39	    #pragma unroll
40	    for (int j = 0; j < H; j++) {
41	        float h = W1[j] * abs_grad + b1[j];
42	        h = (h > 0.0f) ? h : 0.0f;       // ReLU
43	        h_acc += W2[j] * h;
44	    }
45	    return h_acc + b2;
46	}
47	
48	// Apply: g_amp = (s * alpha + beta) * g, then run AdamW on g_amp.
49	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
50	__device__ __forceinline__ void neuralgrok_apply_step(
51	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
52	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
53	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
54	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
55	    const float psi_scale,        // output of psi_net forward
56	    const float alpha,
57	    const float beta,
58	    const float lr,
59	    const float beta1,
60	    const float beta2,
61	    const float eps,
62	    const float wd,
63	    const float bc1,
64	    const float bc2,
65	    const int64_t idx,
66	    const float clip_coef = 1.0f   // eager GLOBAL grad-norm clip coef (1.0 = inert); applied before psi+amp
67	) {
68	    const float g = static_cast<float>(grad[idx]) * clip_coef;
69	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
70	
71	    const float g_amp = (psi_scale * alpha + beta) * g;
72	
73	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_amp;
74	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp;
75	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
76	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
77	
78	    // bc1, bc2 un-inverted (= 1 - beta^t): divide for bias correction.
79	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
80	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
81	}
82	
83	// Canonical bias-corrected Adam tail on a caller-supplied effective gradient
84	// g_eff. SINGLE source of the moment-update + decoupled-WD apply math, factored
85	// out of neuralgrok_apply_step so the "Adam-only on a pre-amplified gradient"
86	// kernel can reuse the exact same float ops without re-inlining them. Writes
87	// the new moments into exp_avg[idx]/exp_avg_sq[idx] and the new parameter into
88	// param[idx].
89	//
90	// Bit-identical to the tail of neuralgrok_apply_step:
91	//   m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1 - beta1) * g_eff;
92	//   v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1 - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
93	//   update = (m / bc1) / (sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps);
94	//   param[idx] = p - lr * (update + wd * p);
95	template <typename ParamT>
96	__device__ __forceinline__ void neuralgrok_adam_tail(
97	    ParamT* __restrict__ param,
98	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
99	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq,
100	    const float g_eff,
101	    const float lr,
102	    const float beta1,
103	    const float beta2,
104	    const float eps,
105	    const float wd,
106	    const float bc1,
107	    const float bc2,
108	    const int64_t idx
109	) {
110	    const float p = static_cast<float>(param[idx]);
111	    const float m = beta1 * exp_avg[idx]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g_eff;
112	    const float v = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[idx] + (1.0f - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff;
113	    exp_avg[idx]    = m;
114	    exp_avg_sq[idx] = v;
115	    const float update = (m / sg_safe_bc(bc1)) / (sqrtf(v / sg_safe_bc(bc2)) + eps);
116	    param[idx] = static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p));
117	}
118	
119	}} // namespace sg::algorithms
